item.title: Greek New Year Traditions 2026: Vasilopita, Pomegranate Smashing, and Ancient Customs for Good Luck
item.description: At midnight or on New Year's morning, the "lucky" first-footer smashes a pomegranate against the doorstep—the more seeds that scatter, the more luck, health, and prosperity the household will enjoy in the new year. Families then cut the Vasilopita, hunting for the hidden coin that brings blessings to its finder. item.description: Recent 2025 studies at Agios Vasileios reveal Linear B tablets documenting trade and rituals, alongside luxury artifacts preserved by fire—proving Laconia was a thriving Mycenaean palatial state long before classical Sparta's warriors. item.title: Rare Ancient Greek Kore Head Discovered in Etruscan City of Vulci
item.description: Archaeologists have unearthed a rare marble head of an ancient Greek kore in the Etruscan city of Vulci, Italy. Dating to the early 5th century BCE from an Attic workshop, this exceptional find—complete with traces of original paint—provides striking evidence of deep cultural and artistic ties between Greece and Etruria over 2,500 years ago.
